label: copy-phase input token j (fed back after <DEL>)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input fed back is the token j (in_tok == j holds for 100% of activation mass). It never fires during the original phase (j appearing in the original sequence) or at the <DEL> step. It is weak or absent when j is the first token fed back (recall_idx 1, i.e. original token 0 was j): rate 0.6% there vs about 3% at recall_idx >= 2. Restricting to recall_idx >= 2 gives F1 0.92; plain copy-phase j gives F1 0.86 with recall 1.0. Magnitude goes up for later copy positions and longer sequences. The top activations all come at the last copy step of L=9 sequences, where j is fed back after 7 copied tokens. It is not selective for the output token, the next token, or the token before. False positives are mostly j fed back at an early copy position in short sequences.

issues: Minor: the claim 'magnitude goes up for later copy positions and longer sequences' holds only weakly. Activation rate rises from 0.6% at recall_idx 1 to about 3% at recall_idx 2 and then stays flat at 2.7-3.2% for recall_idx 2-8. Mass share by L rises mostly because longer sequences have more steps.

The remaining false positives (precision about 0.88) are spread evenly across subsets. Precision is 0.89 with in_count==1, 0.85 with in_count>=2, 0.91 after a digit, 0.89 at to_go<=2, 0.89 at to_go>=5 and 0.91 at the last step. The one dip is L<=4 (0.69), which covers only about 5% of activations. None of these is a systematic counterexample class.
Missed activations (1.8% of mass) are mostly weak firings when j is the first token fed back (recall_idx 1). This is the documented exclusion, not a gap.

Claims verified: zero activity in the original and delimiter phases. in_tok==j accounts for 100% of activation mass (3 stray hits on h/f). Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.884, R 0.952, F1 0.917, mass recall 0.982. Plain copy-phase j gives F1 0.864 with recall 1.0. Adding L>=5 (F1 0.90), recall_idx>=3 (0.83) or correct==1 (0.919, a negligible gain) does not beat the predicate meaningfully.
